fields.System.Title: RPL-403 — Prioritise tasks blocking a wave
fields.System.Description:
Story

As a supervisor, I want replenishments that a wave is waiting on done first, so that
committed picking work is not held up by a routine top-up elsewhere.

Acceptance criteria

  • - Given a task tied to a released or imminent wave, then it is issued before general
  • replenishment tasks.
  • - Given several wave-blocking tasks, then they are ordered by the wave's cut-off time.
  • - Given priority, then it is recalculated as waves are released and completed, not fixed
  • at creation.
  • - Given a wave-blocking task outstanding when release is attempted, then it is surfaced
  • by [OUT-306](../OUT/OUT-306-block-release-until-replenished.md).
  • - Given the priority scheme, then general tasks are not starved indefinitely.

Traceability

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Modules | replenishment, outbound |
| Tables | replen_task, wave |
| Risks | Replen completing after the wave is picked ([doc 09 §7.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md)); starvation of routine work |
| Tests | unit · integration |
